measured.label: measured
measured.what: Deterministic: an AST, git, or metric tool proved this directly.

metric-anchored.label: metric-anchored judgment
metric-anchored.what: Judgment biased hard by a metric (import graph, fan-in, churn), but still judgment — the metric points; it does not decide.

requires-your-intent.label: requires your intent
requires-your-intent.what: Extrinsic: not in the code. Only a human naming a concern (via /audit-slice) can ground this; a structural pass cannot assert it.

core.what: Load-bearing: the application cannot function without it.
core.how: Proposed from the import graph + metrics: high fan-in, central in the dependency graph, often high churn or complexity. A structural pass PROPOSES this; a slice confirms it.
core.teaches: Core is the last thing to refactor; seam around it before pruning its dependents. Fooled by re-export hubs (high fan-in but trivial) and by product intent — kill a feature and a former-core module can become removable. 'Essential' is partly a product claim, not a pure code fact.

seam.what: A deliberately thin boundary that connects two larger parts.
seam.how: Weakly detectable: small LOC + meaningful fan-in + a Protocol/typed contract HINT at a seam, but DELIBERATENESS is not measurable. A structural pass can only flag a CANDIDATE; intent confirms it.
seam.teaches: Seams weaken connascence and make two sides independently changeable — the target state of a modularize phase. Thinness is measurable; deliberateness and boundary-ness are not, so seam is the most judgment-dependent class to DETECT. Always a candidate ('possible extension point — confirm intent'), never an asserted detection.

removable.what: A strip candidate: dead, superseded, or dead-on-arrival.
removable.how: NOT in the code. Requires a user-stated concern (/audit-slice) that establishes a feature is gone or a path is unused. A structural or LLM pass must NEVER auto-classify removable — it would have to fabricate the intent it was never given.
removable.teaches: Removable is meaningless without intent: 'unused' is relative to a product surface only a human defines. Until a slice grounds it, a removable verdict renders BLANK ('requires your judgment — run /audit-slice'), never as an LLM guess dressed as a finding.

direct-call.what: One component names another's identifier (a call/import).
direct-call.how: Detected statically by the AST import graph (build_import_graph). The strongest evidence the tool has: the caller's source literally contains the callee's name.
direct-call.teaches: Connascence of Name — the weakest, normal form of coupling. Not a smell. Only a problem when the callee is itself removable. Fooled by re-export hubs and __init__ facades that inflate the count.

shared-state.what: Two components both read/write the same data structure.
shared-state.how: Audit-asserted: NOT statically detectable from imports. A human slice must observe both writers touching one global/singleton/DOM node without a single-writer contract.
shared-state.teaches: Connascence of Identity or Value. Tolerable at small scale; corrosive as the structure grows — any shape change forces coordinated edits and out-of-order writes cause silent bugs. Fooled by assuming co-location implies coordination.

background-knowledge.what: An unenforced invariant one component assumes about another.
background-knowledge.how: Requires intent: the invariant lives only in a human's head, an ADR, or a drifting comment. No code, type, or test enforces it, so nothing static can detect it — only a human who knows the contract.
background-knowledge.teaches: Connascence of Convention/Algorithm — the most expensive form, always a smell: the compiler, type checker, and test suite cannot catch a violation. Pruning a removable component that carries one deletes the invariant entirely — the architectural prize.

static.what: The AST/import graph proved this edge.
static.how: Emitted by build_import_graph when an import resolves to a repo file. Renders as a SOLID stroke.
static.teaches: Solid = the tool can prove it. Cannot prove runtime/dynamic coupling (reflection, dependency injection, string-keyed dispatch).

audit-asserted.what: A human asserted this edge from a slice.
audit-asserted.how: Authored during /audit-slice + /synthesize-audit. Renders as a DASHED stroke. As trustworthy as the slice behind it.
audit-asserted.teaches: Dashed = judgment, not proof. Shared-state and background-knowledge edges are always audit-asserted because they are not statically detectable; that is precisely why they are the expensive forms.

direction_encoding.what: Outgoing edges draw full-colour; incoming edges draw lighter.
direction_encoding.how: A renderer convention (opacity + colour-lightness), not data.
direction_encoding.teaches: Direction shows who depends on whom, which drives stability: depend TOWARD more-stable (lower-instability) modules (Stable-Dependencies Principle).

loc.teaches: Size != complexity. A huge file is a prompt to LOOK, not a verdict. Fooled by generated code and long string literals.

fan_in.how: Distinct repo modules that import this one (AST import graph).
fan_in.teaches: High fan-in = widely depended-on, so change is expensive (stability). Fooled by re-export hubs / __init__.

fan_out.how: Distinct repo modules this one imports (AST import graph).
fan_out.teaches: High fan-out = this knows about many things (instability). Fooled by a facade that legitimately wires many parts.

cyclomatic.how: Mean radon cc_visit complexity over blocks; ABSENT if radon is not installed.
cyclomatic.teaches: Branching complexity: hard to test, hard to reason about. When radon is absent this is UNAVAILABLE, not 0 — do not read a missing value as 'simple'.

churn_90d.how: Commits touching the file in the window (git log --since).
churn_90d.teaches: A change magnet: still-evolving or unstable code. Fooled by mass reformatting and renames.

test_ratio.how: Repo test-LOC / source-LOC, attached to modules a test imports (a rollup proxy).
test_ratio.teaches: A repo-level rollup, not per-file truth: import != assertion. Admit the proxy.

instability.how: I = fan_out / (fan_in + fan_out); undefined for isolated nodes.
instability.teaches: Teaches Stable-Dependencies: depend toward lower-I modules. Ignores dynamic coupling; A (abstractness) is not measured, so no main-sequence distance.

refactor_pressure.how: churn * cyclomatic * max(fan_in,1) / max(test_ratio, 0.05); ABSENT if any input (esp. cyclomatic) is missing.
refactor_pressure.teaches: Biases attention to hot/complex/depended/untested code — 'look here first', never 'refactor this'. None if any input is missing (fully absent when radon is).

glossary.definition: How much one component must know about another. Surfaced directly as fan-in (importers) + fan-out (imports) — counts of import edges.
glossary.proxy_honesty: Direct for static imports; blind to runtime coupling.

glossary.definition: How single-purpose a module is (one reason to change). The tool does NOT ship a measured cohesion metric: a clean code-intrinsic proxy (within-file vs cross-file reference ratio) is not available from the file-level import graph, and len(logical_owners) is judgment-derived (authored by synthesis), not substrate — presenting it as 'measured' would dress judgment as measurement.
glossary.proxy_honesty: No measured proxy here by design. Read it qualitatively: a file owned by many logical components (a synthesis judgment) hints at low cohesion, but that is a verdict, not a number.

glossary.definition: Reducing what two components must know about each other, usually by inserting a seam (a typed boundary). The seam classification marks where this has been done deliberately.
glossary.proxy_honesty: Seam-ness is judgment; only thinness (LOC) is measured.

glossary.definition: I = fan_out / (fan_in + fan_out), in [0,1]. I=0 is maximally stable (a depended-on sink); I=1 is maximally unstable (a leaf).
glossary.proxy_honesty: Exact for static imports. Abstractness A (the other axis of the main sequence) is not reliably computable in Python, so the tool surfaces I but NOT main-sequence distance — and says so.

glossary.definition: Resistance to change. Proxied by low instability + high fan-in: many dependents make a module expensive to change.
glossary.proxy_honesty: Partial — stability is also about change RATE; pair with churn_90d. A low-I module that churns constantly is not really stable.

glossary.definition: A module should have one reason to change. Proxied by many logical owners (judgment) plus high churn — many owners changing often approximates many reasons to change.
glossary.proxy_honesty: Weak proxy: churn counts commits, not distinct REASONS; a mass reformat inflates it. The owner count is a judgment, not a metric.

glossary.definition: The dependency graph should have no cycles. Detected exactly by Tarjan strongly-connected-components over the static import graph; any component in a cycle of size >1 is flagged.
glossary.proxy_honesty: Strong — SCC is exact for STATIC imports. A cycle formed only through runtime/dynamic dispatch is invisible to it.

glossary.definition: Dependencies should point toward more-stable (lower-I) components. Read the instability gradient along an edge: depending on a more unstable module than yourself is the violation.
glossary.proxy_honesty: Proxy via the I gradient; ignores dynamic coupling.

glossary.definition: Two components are connascent if a change in one forces a change in the other. Strength taxonomy (weak→strong): Name → Type → Meaning/Convention → Position → Algorithm → Execution-Order → Timing → Identity. The three edge types map onto it: direct-call = Name/Type (weakest), shared-state = Identity/Value, background-knowledge = Convention/Algorithm (strongest).
glossary.proxy_honesty: Name/Type are detected exactly (AST imports). Convention/Algorithm cannot be measured at all — which is WHY they are the most expensive forms. Locality and other forms have no proxy here.

glossary.definition: A deep module hides a lot of implementation behind a narrow interface (high LOC, low fan-in is a hint). A shallow module adds little behind a wide interface (low LOC, high fan-out is a hint).
glossary.proxy_honesty: Weak proxy: interface NARROWNESS is not directly measured. LOC and fan counts are only hints — a file can be large and shallow.

logical_components.name: ApiRouter
logical_components.description: HTTP entrypoint. Parses requests, dispatches to the store, loads plugins. The application's front door.

logical_components.name: Store
logical_components.description: In-memory + persisted record store. Read and written by multiple callers; the shared-state hub of the service.

logical_components.name: PluginLoader
logical_components.description: Discovers and instantiates external plugins against a typed Protocol. The intended extension seam.

logical_components.name: LegacyExport
logical_components.description: Old CSV export path superseded by the plugin system. Still wired into the router but no longer used by any live caller. STRIP candidate.

edges.evidence: Both router request handlers and the background flush task read/write Store.records without a single-writer contract.
src/router.py:118 — legacy /export route still calls legacy_export.write_csv
legacy_export assumes Store records are already flushed before it reads them; nothing in code, types, or tests enforces that ordering — the invariant lives only in the original author's head.
Store.flush() calls back into the router refresh hook, closing an import cycle with api-router.

prune_candidates.latent_bug_fixed: The background-knowledge flush-ordering invariant disappears once legacy-export is gone — no remaining caller depends on it.

core_boundary.rationale: Core is the request/store path every feature needs. The seam is the plugin loader (weakest connascence: Name + Type via the Protocol). Removable is the legacy export, kept alive only by one router route, with a background-knowledge edge to the store that is the architectural prize for pruning.
open_questions: store (today core; could become a seam if persistence is made host-injectable)
